subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the full name of Component 1 in CCEA GCSE Music?
questions.explain: Component 1 of the CCEA GCSE Music specification is titled 'Performing and Appraising'.

questions.q: What proportion of the overall CCEA GCSE Music qualification does Component 1 contribute?
questions.explain: Component 1: Performing and Appraising is weighted at 35% of the total qualification.

questions.q: Who assesses a candidate's performances in Component 1?
options: The candidate's own class teacher only
A visiting examiner appointed by CCEA
questions.explain: Performances are externally assessed by a visiting examiner appointed by CCEA.

questions.q: How many separate performances must a candidate present in Component 1?
questions.explain: Candidates present two performances: one solo and one ensemble.

questions.q: In a solo performance, the candidate performs as which of the following?
options: A member of a large choir only
A backing accompanist to another soloist
questions.explain: A solo performance features the candidate as the individual soloist, possibly with accompaniment.

questions.q: A candidate sings a song while a teacher plays the piano accompaniment. How is this classified?
questions.explain: A soloist supported by an accompanist is assessed as a solo, since the accompaniment is not an independent assessed part.

questions.q: 'Intonation' in a solo performance refers to which quality?
options: Playing or singing accurately in tune
The overall speed of the music
questions.explain: Intonation describes how accurately the performer plays or sings in tune.

questions.q: 'Interpretation' is assessed in performance. Which best describes it?
options: Expressive choices such as dynamics, phrasing and tempo
The number of notes played per minute
The physical size of the instrument
The date the piece was composed
questions.explain: Interpretation covers the expressive and musical choices a performer makes to shape the music.

questions.q: A candidate wants to demonstrate strong technical control in a solo. Which feature best shows this?
options: Accurate notes with secure rhythm and clear articulation
Playing everything at one fixed volume
questions.explain: Technical control is shown through accuracy, secure rhythm and clear articulation.

questions.q: What is the minimum requirement for an ensemble performance?
options: The candidate plus at least one other performer
questions.explain: An ensemble requires the candidate to perform together with at least one other performer.

questions.q: For the ensemble mark, the candidate's own part must be which of the following?
options: Doubled exactly by another player throughout
Significant and independent enough to be assessed
The loudest part at all times
questions.explain: The candidate's ensemble part must be independent and significant so their contribution can be judged.

questions.q: Which skill is uniquely tested in an ensemble but not in an unaccompanied solo?
options: Keeping in time and balance with other performers
questions.explain: Ensemble performance additionally assesses coordination, timing and balance with other players.

questions.q: 'Balance' in an ensemble performance refers to which of the following?
options: Adjusting volume so each part can be heard appropriately
questions.explain: Balance means controlling relative volumes so parts blend and the important lines are heard.

questions.q: Why is it important for ensemble members to maintain a steady, shared pulse?
options: So the performers stay together and coordinated
So only the candidate can be heard
questions.explain: A shared, steady pulse keeps the ensemble synchronised and coordinated.

questions.q: A candidate performs the second violin part in a string quartet. How is this best classified?
questions.explain: Playing an independent part within a quartet is an ensemble performance.

questions.q: During an ensemble piece a candidate consistently rushes ahead of the others. Which aspect most needs improvement?
options: Ensemble timing and awareness of the other players
The tuning of a single note
questions.explain: Rushing ahead is a timing and ensemble-awareness issue rather than a solo technical fault.

questions.q: In the appraising discussion, what does the candidate mainly talk about?
options: A piece they have never heard
questions.explain: The appraising discussion focuses on the candidate discussing their own solo and ensemble performances.

questions.q: With whom does the candidate hold the appraising discussion?
questions.explain: The appraising discussion takes place between the candidate and the visiting examiner.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the appraising discussion?
options: To show understanding of the music performed and how it was prepared
To rehearse for a future concert
To compose a new piece on the spot
questions.explain: It allows candidates to demonstrate musical understanding of the works they performed and their preparation.

questions.q: An examiner asks a candidate to describe features of their solo. Which response best fits the appraising discussion?
options: Discussing its structure, dynamics, tempo and the challenges faced
Refusing to comment on the music
questions.explain: A strong appraisal describes musical features and performance challenges of the pieces performed.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Music (2017) specification; Component 1: Performing and Appraising
